{{short description|Mathematical constants}}
The '''Beraha constants''' are a series of [[mathematical constant]]s by which the  <math>n\text{th}</math> Beraha constant is given by

: <math>B (n) = 2 + 2 \cos \left ( \frac{2\pi}{n} \right ).</math>

Notable examples of Beraha constants include <math>B (5)</math> is <math>\varphi + 1</math>, where <math>\varphi</math> is the [[golden ratio]], <math>B (7)</math> is the '''silver constant'''<!--boldface per WP:R#PLA--><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/SilverConstant.html|title=Silver Constant|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|date=|website=Wolfram MathWorld|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=November 3, 2018}}</ref> (also known as the '''silver root'''<!--boldface per WP:R#PLA-->),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/SilverRoot.html|title=Silver Root|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|date=|website=Wolfram MathWorld|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 5, 2020}}</ref> and <math>B (10) = \varphi + 2</math>.
